// Adds the "in-webview" class to the <html /> element if the user is detected
// to be in a webview.
function checkForWebview() {
  const ua = navigator.userAgent || window.opera
  const isNewsIOSAppWebview = /nytios/i.test(ua)
  const isNewsAndroidAppWebview = /nyt_android/i.test(ua)
  const isCookingIOSAppWebview = /\bCooking\//i.test(ua)
  const isCookingAndroidAppWebview = /NYTCooking\//i.test(ua)
  const isInAppWebview = isNewsIOSAppWebview || isNewsAndroidAppWebview || isCookingIOSAppWebview || isCookingAndroidAppWebview
  if (isInAppWebview) {
    document.documentElement.classList.add("in-webview");
  }

class="pantry--title-section-alternate sectionheader_title__5aon0">FAQS</h2><ol><li class="faq_faqItem__c5ipW"><div class="faq_faqItemContainer__NoLC8"><h3 class="pantry--ui-lg-strong faq_faqQuestionContainer__bmed2"><button aria-controls=":R64tlan6:" aria-expanded="true" class="faq_faqQuestionButton__LFUao">How to make beef stew on the stove<span class="faq_chevronIcon__jBoas faq_expanded__awl0n"><svg width="14" height="10" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="m14 2.205-7 7-7-7L1.41.795 7 6.385l5.59-5.59L14 2.205Z" fill="#000"></path></svg></span></button></h3><div id=":R64tlan6:" aria-hidden="false" class="faq_faqAnswerContainer__CDKnK faq_expanded__awl0n"><div class="faq_faqAnswerContent__aoaU6"><p class="pantry--body-long">It’s important to cook stew slowly over low heat. High heat will cause the meat to tighten and toughen, while low heat allows the meat to become fall-apart tender. Simply cover the pot, leaving a small gap for steam to escape, and keep the heat as low as it goes.</p></div></div></div></li><li class="faq_faqItem__c5ipW"><div class="faq_faqItemContainer__NoLC8"><h3 class="pantry--ui-lg-strong faq_faqQuestionContainer__bmed2"><button aria-controls=":Ra4tlan6:" aria-expanded="false" class="faq_faqQuestionButton__LFUao">How to cook beef stew in a slow cooker<span class="faq_chevronIcon__jBoas"><svg width="14" height="10" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="m14 2.205-7 7-7-7L1.41.795 7 6.385l5.59-5.59L14 2.205Z" fill="#000"></path></svg></span></button></h3><div id=":Ra4tlan6:" aria-hidden="true" class="faq_faqAnswerContainer__CDKnK"><div class="faq_faqAnswerContent__aoaU6"><p class="pantry--body-long">For additional ease, beef stew can be prepared in a slow cooker or crock pot. You can try a slow cooker variation of beef stew in <a href="https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1019691-slow-cooker-beef-stew">this recipe</a> or prepare any beef stew through the step when everything is simmering together, then transfer to a slow cooker and continue cooking until the meat is tender.</p></div></div></div></li><li class="faq_faqItem__c5ipW"><div class="faq_faqItemContainer__NoLC8"><h3 class="pantry--ui-lg-strong faq_faqQuestionContainer__bmed2"><button aria-controls=":Re4tlan6:" aria-expanded="false" class="faq_faqQuestionButton__LFUao">What to serve with beef stew<span class="faq_chevronIcon__jBoas"><svg width="14" height="10" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="m14 2.205-7 7-7-7L1.41.795 7 6.385l5.59-5.59L14 2.205Z" fill="#000"></path></svg></span></button></h3><div id=":Re4tlan6:" aria-hidden="true" class="faq_faqAnswerContainer__CDKnK"><div class="faq_faqAnswerContent__aoaU6"><p class="pantry--body-long">The best accompaniments to beef stew can soak up the sauce. A crusty baguette works well, as does rice. A beef stew is hearty enough to be a one-pot meal, but you can make a salad with some crisp, fresh vegetables.</p></div></div></div></li><li class="faq_faqItem__c5ipW"><div class="faq_faqItemContainer__NoLC8"><h3 class="pantry--ui-lg-strong faq_faqQuestionContainer__bmed2"><button aria-controls=":Ri4tlan6:" aria-expanded="false" class="faq_faqQuestionButton__LFUao">How to thicken beef stew<span class="faq_chevronIcon__jBoas"><svg width="14" height="10" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="m14 2.205-7 7-7-7L1.41.795 7 6.385l5.59-5.59L14 2.205Z" fill="#000"></path></svg></span></button></h3><div id=":Ri4tlan6:" aria-hidden="true" class="faq_faqAnswerContainer__CDKnK"><div class="faq_faqAnswerContent__aoaU6"><p class="pantry--body-long">Starches, like the flour, cornstarch and potatoes, thicken beef stew. Sometimes, beef cubes are coated in flour, then browned, leaving flour in the pan while sealing flour to the meat. When the meat is later simmered, that flour thickens the liquid as do potatoes, which release their starches as they cook.
